novelty.justification: The claim’s novelty route is a typology-based mechanism hypothesis: “typological features of that language (morphological richness, word order, numeral systems, tense/aspect marking) systematically predict reasoning performance on structurally-matched tasks,” rather than merely observing multilingual accuracy gaps. Searches using “multilingual chain-of-thought reasoning language typology,” “reasoning language affects LLM accuracy,” and “linguistic relativity numeral systems LLM reasoning” identify the closest work as A Comprehensive Evaluation of Multilingual Chain-of-Thought Reasoning (2025), which already studies target-language performance and interchanges reasoning traces across languages, alongside Long Chain-of-Thought Reasoning Across Languages (2025) and Tokenization Constraints in LLMs (2025). Moving from those studies to attributing task-specific error patterns jointly to numeral transparency, word order, morphology, and tense/aspect is a substantive multi-step integration and new unit of analysis, but it remains a natural extension of established multilingual-CoT disparities and linguistic-relativity questions rather than a wholly new core paradigm.
